title: Jonah and the Inheritance
premise: When estate lawyer Ansel Lockridge is handed a second will from town founder Edmund Voss—dated after his death and naming an unknown heir—the document should be impossible. Ansel's investigation collides with the exhumation ordered by Voss's resentful grandson, which reveals the founder's coffin has been empty for decades. Digging through thirty-year-old alibis, Ansel uncovers that Voss faked his death to escape blackmail by the town council he'd built, living out his last years in secret with the woman he loved, his housekeeper Ruth. The final will leaves everything to Ruth's daughter, but the councilmen who helped bury the secret have been silencing witnesses ever since. In the climax, Ansel traps the last surviving conspirator into confessing at the reopened grave, and the inheritance passes—not as money, but as the truth that finally frees the town.
about_author: Coral Joubert spent a decade clerking in probate courts before turning to fiction, giving her mysteries an insider's eye for paperwork that lies. She writes from a converted notary office on the coast of Maine, where every small town she invents hides something worth exhuming.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Ansel Lockridge, POV. A courier delivers a will dated six months after Edmund Voss's death, naming an heir no one can find. Ansel, who prides themselves on closable cases, almost refuses—until they notice the notary stamp belongs to their own late mentor. Beat: professional pride curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Terms of Probate
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. At the Voss estate reading, grandson Julian Voss demands the will be declared fraudulent; the housekeeper Ruth Ashford watches silently from the doorway. Ansel notices fresh flowers on a mantel no servant admits tending. Beat: the family's grief masks old, well-practiced resentments.

chapters.title: Ground Order
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian forces through an exhumation petition, claiming the second will proves the body was never verified. His lawyer warns him what he might find. Julian doesn't care—he wants the empire back. Beat: ambition dressed up as filial duty.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Held
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. At the exhumation, the coffin opens on weighted sandbags and a stranger's funeral suit. The crowd gasps; Ruth turns and walks away without a word. Ansel pockets a monogrammed cufflink from the soil. Beat: shock hardening into resolve—the case just became personal.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. Ansel pulls the death certificate, autopsy report, and burial permits, finding identical signatures from three men: the coroner, the mayor, and the bank president—all still alive or recently dead. Every alibi is airtight because it was written by the same hand. Beat: the thrill of a pattern emerging.

chapters.title: Ruth's Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth POV. Ruth remembers Edmund alive in the cottage by the marsh, laughing again for the first time in years, and the promise she made to keep him dead. She burns a letter when she hears Ansel is asking questions. Beat: love against duty, told from inside the secret.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. The retired coroner, drunk and frightened, shows Ansel a ledger page torn out the week of the burial. He admits he certified a body he never examined—for money, and because Mayor Pell showed him photographs. Beat: fear revealing that this conspiracy protected someone, not something.

chapters.title: Photographs
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. The photographs show Edmund Voss alive, years past his death date, embracing a woman whose face is turned away. Ansel recognizes the cottage from Ruth's window curtains. Beat: tenderness discovered at the center of a crime.

chapters.title: Julian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian finds his grandfather's real accounting books: payments to three town officials for thirty years, labeled only 'the arrangement.' He realizes the fortune he inherited was hush money—and that whoever killed the payments may want him gone too. Beat: inheritance revealed as a leash.

chapters.title: The Bank President Dies
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. Harold Finch, the third signatory, dies in an apparent fall hours before Ansel's appointment with him. Police call it accidental. Ansel finds Finch's calendar marked with Ansel's name and one word: 'before.' Beat: dread—the conspirators are closing ranks.

chapters.title: Mayor Pell's Version
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. Mayor Pell, now elderly and untouchable, gives Ansel tea and a polished story: Edmund died abroad, the town buried a stand-in to spare his fragile legacy. It's almost believable—until Pell mentions the woman in the photographs by name, a name he was never shown. Beat: the mask slipping, menace under courtesy.

chapters.title: Daughter of the House
chapters.summary: Maren POV. Maren Ashford, Ruth's daughter, a nurse who left town at eighteen, returns when her mother stops answering calls. She finds the burned letter's fragments in the grate and reads her own name in the will's beneficiary line. Beat: a life built on a lie cracking open.

chapters.title: The Cottage by the Marsh
chapters.summary: Ansel and Maren POV, alternating. Following the cufflink and curtain detail, they search the marsh cottage and find Edmund's true deathbed: medicine bottles dated four years ago, a journal, and two coffins' worth of digging in the garden. Beat: intimacy with the dead man's hidden happiness, shadowed by who else knew.

chapters.title: The Journal
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. Edmund's journal names his blackmailer: not the council, but his own son—Julian's father—who discovered the embezzlement that built the Voss fortune and traded silence for control. Edmund faked his death to escape his own blood. Beat: power's corruption traced to its root.

chapters.title: What Ruth Kept
chapters.summary: Ruth POV. Ruth confesses to Maren: she helped bury the empty coffin because Edmund begged her, and she has spent thirty years being paid in secrets. She kept the original will hidden because publishing it would have made Maren a target. Beat: duty and love finally at war in one heart.

chapters.title: Fire at the Records Office
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. The county archive burns overnight, destroying the burial permits. Ansel had photographed everything; the arsonist doesn't know it. But the fire's timing means someone inside the case is reporting to Pell—or to whoever Pell answers to now. Beat: the enemy adapts faster than expected.

chapters.title: Julian's Choice
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Pell offers Julian the empire intact if he withdraws the probate challenge and lets the second will burn. Julian, holding his grandfather's journal pages, realizes he's being recruited into the same arrangement that owned his father. Beat: the heir deciding whether to become the next corruptor.

chapters.title: Before the Grave
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. Ansel arranges a public reinterment ceremony, inviting Pell, Julian, Ruth, and the press—an exhumation in reverse, with the whole town watching. They rebury the cufflink and read the second will aloud over open ground. Beat: turning secrecy into spectacle, setting the trap.

chapters.title: Pell Breaks
chapters.summary: Climax, Ansel POV. Before the crowd and a hidden recorder, Ansel springs the name error from Chapter 11: Pell could only know the woman's identity if he'd seen Edmund alive. Cornered before the town that worshipped him, Pell confesses to the false burial and implicates Finch's killer—his own fixer, still on his payroll. Beat: confession as collapse.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Maren POV. Pell and his fixer are taken; Julian hands the state his grandfather's ledgers, choosing truth over inheritance. Maren stands at the grave of the man who was her father in every way but paper, while Ruth finally weeps in public. Beat: grief allowed at last.

chapters.title: Probate Closed
chapters.summary: Ansel POV. In court, the second will is validated; the estate passes to Maren, who converts the Voss holdings into a public trust and keeps only the marsh cottage. Ansel closes the file—the one case they couldn't close cleanly, and the better for it. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Flowers on the Mantel
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ansel POV. Months later, Ansel visits the cottage and finds fresh flowers on the mantel—Ruth's ritual, continued freely now. On the desk lies Edmund's last journal page: 'Let them think me dead. I finally lived.' Ansel leaves the door unlocked. Beat: peace earned, love outlasting duty.
